script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Good morning, Fernwell Cycle Hire, Jenny speaking. How can I help you?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Oh, hi. I'm visiting the area with my wife next month, and we'd like to hire a couple of bikes for a weekend. Is that something I can book over the phone?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Yes, of course. I'll just take a few details and fill in a booking form for you. Could I have your name first, please?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Sure. It's Marcus. Marcus Talbridge.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Could you spell the surname for me?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Yep, it's T-A-L-B-R-I-D-G-E.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Lovely, thank you. Now, what kind of bikes were you thinking of? We have road bikes, mountain bikes and hybrids.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Well, I did think about mountain bikes, because I've heard there are some hills around here. But we'll mostly be on country lanes and the old railway path, so I think a mountain bike would be a bit heavy for that.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: That's right. Most people doing the lanes go for a hybrid. They're light, but the tyres are a bit wider than on a road bike, so they cope with gravel.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: OK, then let's go for hybrids. Two of them, please.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Two hybrids. And which weekend would that be?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: We arrive on Friday the nineteenth of June, so we'd want them on the Saturday, the twentieth. Oh, hang on, no. Sorry, I'm looking at the wrong week on my calendar. We get there on the twentieth, so it's Saturday the twenty-first. And we'd bring them back on the Sunday evening.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: So the twenty-first and twenty-second. No problem. What time would you like to collect them on the Saturday? We open at eight.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Could we say eight o'clock? Actually, no, we'll need breakfast first. Let's make it half past eight.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Eight thirty, fine. Now, do you need any extras? We have helmets, which are free, and you can add bags, locks and so on.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: We'll bring our own helmets. But we'll be carrying a picnic and some spare clothes. Do you have baskets?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: We normally do, but I'm afraid all our baskets are booked for that weekend. What I can offer instead is panniers. They're the bags that clip on to a rack at the back of the bike.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Oh, panniers would be even better, actually. Can we have one on each bike?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Yes, I'll put down two panniers. Do you know which route you'll be taking? We give out free route maps.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Someone at our hotel mentioned the Heron Trail along the river.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Ah, I'm sorry to say part of the Heron Trail is closed at the moment, because the river bank collapsed in the winter. Most people are doing the Kestrel Trail instead. It goes up through the woods and comes back past the lake.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: The Kestrel Trail. Is that K-E-S-T-R-E-L?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: That's it. I'll put a Kestrel Trail map in with your booking.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Great. So, how much is all of this going to cost?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Let me see. Hybrids are twenty-five pounds a day, so two bikes for two days would be a hundred. Oh, no, wait. For a whole weekend we have a special rate, which is forty pounds per bike. So that's eighty for the two bikes.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: And the panniers?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Panniers are three pounds each, so six pounds altogether. That brings the total to eighty-six pounds.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: That sounds reasonable. Do I pay now?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: You pay the hire charge when you collect the bikes, but we do ask for a deposit of twenty pounds to hold the booking. We can't take cash for the deposit, I'm afraid, so it would need to be by credit card.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: No problem. I'll give you the card details at the end.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Thanks. Just a couple more questions. We like to know how customers hear about us. Was it our website, or perhaps a leaflet?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Neither, actually. There's a cycling podcast I listen to, and the presenter mentioned you in an episode about the region.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Oh, how nice! I'll make a note of that. And lastly, when you come to collect the bikes, you'll need to show some photo ID. We don't accept bank statements or bills any more, so it has to be a driving licence or a passport.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Well, my licence is Australian, so I'll just bring my passport. That's easier.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.text: Perfect. Right, if you can read me the card number now, I'll take the deposit.

questions.explanation: The caller spells his surname T-A-L-B-R-I-D-G-E.
He considers mountain bikes but decides they are too heavy and chooses hybrids.
He first says the 20th, then corrects himself: Saturday the twenty-first.
Eight o'clock is rejected because of breakfast; he chooses half past eight.
Baskets are all booked, so he takes panniers, one per bike.
The Heron Trail is partly closed, so the map is for the Kestrel Trail.
The weekend rate gives £80 for two bikes, plus £6 for panniers: £86. The first figure of £100 is corrected.
Cash is not accepted for the deposit; it must be paid by credit card.
Not the website or a leaflet, but a cycling podcast.
Bills are not accepted; he decides to bring his passport rather than his licence.
